name: Renogy 1000W Pure Sine Inverter
description: A 12V, 1,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 2,000W peak, the right size for laptops, TVs, CPAPs and small fridges in vans, trucks and cabins.
quick: 12V DC in, 1,000W continuous, pure sine. A 12V, 1,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 2,000W peak, the right size for laptops, TVs, CPAPs and small fridges in vans, trucks and cabins.
bestFor: Vans, trucks and cabins running laptops, TVs and small fridges
skipIf: You want to run a microwave or coffee maker
verdict: If you are not sure what size inverter you need, a 1,000W pure sine unit is the safest bet, and Renogy's is the one most people end up with.

**Size it to your loads.** Renogy rates it at 1,000W continuous and 2,000W peak from a 12V battery. That runs a laptop (65W), a TV (100W), a CPAP (30-60W), a blender (500W) or a small fridge with its startup surge. It will not run a 1,000W microwave, which actually draws about 1,500W from the wall; that needs the [Renogy 2000W](/gear/renogy-2000w-pure-sine-inverter/).

**The wiring stays manageable.** Current is watts divided by volts, plus losses. At full load: 1,000W / 12V / 0.9 efficiency is about 93 amps. That is a short run of heavy cable and a correctly sized fuse at the battery, not the 200-amp problem of a 2,000W unit. Renogy lists nominal efficiency above 90%.

**Clean power and simple outputs.** The output is a [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/), so motors, chargers and medical devices run cool and quiet. It has 2 AC outlets and a 5V/2.1A USB port. Renogy also makes the batteries, charge controllers and DC-DC chargers that usually sit beside an inverter, which makes a matched van or trailer system simple. To estimate battery runtime, use our [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) with your battery's [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/).

Owners praise its quiet output and solid build. The common complaint is fan noise under heavy load. It is the top pick in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide; the [Victron Phoenix 12/1200](/gear/victron-phoenix-12-1200-inverter/) is the premium alternative for always-on use.
pros: Pure sine output for sensitive electronics
About 93A at full load keeps cabling reasonable
Fits Renogy's battery and solar ecosystem
cons: Not enough for microwaves or coffee makers
Fan can be noisy under heavy load

faqs.q: Can the Renogy 1000W inverter run a microwave?
faqs.a: Usually not. A microwave rated at 1,000W of cooking power draws about 1,400 to 1,600W from the outlet, which exceeds this inverter's 1,000W continuous rating. The 2,000W peak only covers brief startup surges. For a microwave, step up to a 2,000W pure sine inverter and a battery bank that can supply about 185 amps.

faqs.q: What size fuse and cable does the Renogy 1000W inverter need?
faqs.a: Plan for about 93 amps at full load from a 12V battery (1,000W / 12V / 0.9 efficiency). That calls for heavy-gauge cable on a short run and a fuse at the battery sized to protect that cable. Follow Renogy's manual for the exact gauge and fuse rating for your cable length.

name: GoWISE Power PS1003 2000W Inverter
amazon: GoWISE Power PS1003 2000W pure sine wave inverter
description: A 12V, 2,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 4,000W peak, 3 AC outlets and a remote switch, the value pick for microwaves and jobsite tools.
quick: 12V DC in, 2,000W continuous, pure sine. A 12V, 2,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 4,000W peak, 3 AC outlets and a remote switch, the value pick for microwaves and jobsite tools.
bestFor: Microwaves, coffee makers and corded tools off a big battery bank
skipIf: Your battery or BMS cannot deliver 200 amps
verdict: The GoWISE PS1003 is the value 2,000W pure sine inverter, and it delivers real kitchen and jobsite capability as long as your battery bank and cabling are built to feed it.

**What 2,000W runs.** GoWISE rates it at 2,000W continuous and 4,000W peak. That covers a 1,000W-class microwave (about 1,500W at the wall), a drip coffee maker, a corded circular saw or a small air compressor's start-up surge. It has 3 AC outlets (not GFCI-protected), a 5V USB port, and a remote on/off switch with cable in the box, so you can mount it near the battery and switch it from the cab.

**Current is the catch.** The GoWISE manual lists 200 amps of input at 12V for full output. That calls for heavy cable on a very short run, a fuse sized to that cable, and a battery bank that can actually deliver 200 amps for minutes at a time. A single small lead-acid battery will sag and trip the low-voltage alarm. A 100Ah lithium battery with a 100A BMS will shut off. Two lithium batteries in parallel, or one with a 200A BMS, is the realistic minimum.

**Runtime math.** A 1,500W microwave for 5 minutes uses about 125Wh, or roughly 12% of a 100Ah 12V lithium battery. Try your own loads in the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/). The output is a [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/).

Owners like the price and the included remote. The common complaints are a loud fan and a USB port that some report failing. It is the 2,000W pick in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide; the [Renogy 2000W](/gear/renogy-2000w-pure-sine-inverter/) is its closest rival.
cons: Draws about 200A at full load from 12V

faqs.q: What battery do I need for the GoWISE 2000W inverter?
faqs.a: One that can supply about 200 amps. GoWISE lists 200A of 12V input at full output. A single 100Ah lithium battery with a 100A BMS will shut off under that load. Use two lithium batteries in parallel, a battery with a 200A BMS, or a large lead-acid bank, with short heavy cables and a correctly sized fuse.

faqs.q: Can the GoWISE PS1003 run a microwave?
faqs.a: Yes. It is rated at 2,000W continuous, and a typical 1,000W microwave draws about 1,500W from the outlet. Five minutes of cooking uses roughly 125Wh, about 12% of a 100Ah 12V lithium battery. The battery and cabling must handle the 150 to 200 amp draw.

name: Victron Phoenix 12/1200
description: Victron's 12V, 1,200VA pure sine inverter with ECO mode and a VE.Direct port, the premium pick for full-time vans and boats where idle draw matters.
quick: 12V DC in, 1,200VA, pure sine. Victron's 12V, 1,200VA pure sine inverter with ECO mode and a VE.Direct port, the premium pick for full-time vans and boats where idle draw matters.
bestFor: Full-time vans and boats that leave the inverter on all day
skipIf: You only need occasional weekend power from a truck
specs: VE.Direct port, ECO mode, remote on/off connector
verdict: Victron is the brand van builders and marine electricians reach for when they want an inverter that runs for a decade, and the Phoenix 12/1200 is its mainstream 12V model.

**Read the rating correctly.** Victron rates it at 1,200VA, which works out to about 1,000W of continuous real power at 25°C, and up to 2,200W peak. On paper that matches the [Renogy 1000W](/gear/renogy-1000w-pure-sine-wave-inverter/). Like all inverters, it delivers a little less continuous power in a hot engine bay, so give it airflow.

**Idle draw is the reason to pay more.** An inverter left on around the clock to power a fridge or router burns energy even with nothing plugged in. ECO mode drops the Phoenix into a search state until a load appears, checking every few seconds, so its standby draw falls to a watt or two. Over a day that saves tens of [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/), which matters on a 100Ah battery.

**Built for a system.** The VE.Direct port links it to Victron's app (with a Bluetooth dongle) and monitoring gear, so you can set low-voltage cut-off, output voltage and ECO thresholds. A remote on/off connector lets you switch it from inside. The output is a clean [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/) from a toroidal transformer design that tolerates hard-starting loads.

Owners praise its reliability and silent idle. The main complaint is the price compared with budget 1,000W units. It is the premium van pick in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide; the [Victron Phoenix 12/800](/gear/victron-phoenix-12-800/) is the smaller sibling.
pros: ECO mode cuts standby draw to a watt or two
Up to 2,200W peak for hard-starting loads
VE.Direct port for app monitoring and settings
cons: Costs far more than budget 1,000W units
App access needs a separate Bluetooth dongle

faqs.q: Is the Victron Phoenix 12/1200 worth it over a cheaper 1000W inverter?
faqs.a: If you leave the inverter on all day, yes. Its ECO mode drops standby draw to about a watt or two, which saves tens of watt-hours a day on a small battery. It also offers app control through VE.Direct. For a truck used on weekends, a budget pure sine inverter does the same job.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Victron Phoenix 12/1200 and 12/800?
faqs.a: Both are 12V pure sine Phoenix inverters with ECO mode and VE.Direct. The 12/1200 is rated at 1,200VA (about 1,000W) with a 2,200W peak. The 12/800 is rated at 800VA (about 650W) with a 1,500W peak, and it draws less current, so it needs lighter cabling.

name: AIMS Power 3000W Pure Sine Inverter
description: A 12V, 3,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 6,000W peak, built for work trucks running miter saws, compressors and battery chargers from an auxiliary bank.
quick: 12V DC in, 3,000W continuous, pure sine. A 12V, 3,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 6,000W peak, built for work trucks running miter saws, compressors and battery chargers from an auxiliary bank.
bestFor: Work trucks running corded tools from an auxiliary battery bank
skipIf: You cannot install a dedicated battery bank and heavy cabling
verdict: Contractors who want corded tools off the truck end up in the 3,000W class, and AIMS Power is one of the established names there.

**What it runs.** AIMS rates it at 3,000W continuous and 6,000W peak, with efficiency around 90% at full load. That covers a miter saw, a small air compressor and a battery charger, or a microwave and coffee maker together. The 6,000W peak helps with motor start-up surges, which can briefly hit two to three times running watts.

**Feeding it is the engineering problem.** At full output, 3,000W / 12V / 0.9 is roughly 280 amps. That needs very short runs of the heaviest cable, a properly rated fuse at the battery, and an auxiliary battery bank isolated from the truck's starting battery. AIMS lists a 9.5-16V DC input window, and the inverter shuts down at the low end. Run it off the starting battery with the engine off and you will be calling for a jump.

**Keep the bank charged.** A DC-DC charger or high-output alternator keeps the house bank topped up while you drive. For runtime math, a 1,500W saw running 10 minutes an hour uses about 250Wh per hour of work; plug your own numbers into the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/). The output is a [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/), so tool chargers and variable-speed tools run correctly.

Owners report it handles real tool loads. Common complaints are fan noise and weight. It is the work-truck pick in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide; most van builds are better served by the [GoWISE 2000W](/gear/gowise-power-2000w-pure-sine-wave-inverter/).
pros: Pure sine output for tool chargers
Runs saws and compressors together with chargers
cons: Needs its own isolated battery bank

faqs.q: Can I run the AIMS 3000W inverter from my truck's starting battery?
faqs.a: Not safely. At full output it draws roughly 280 amps from 12V, which drains a starting battery in minutes and can leave you unable to crank the engine. Install an auxiliary battery bank isolated from the starter battery, charged by a DC-DC charger or a high-output alternator.

faqs.q: Will the AIMS 3000W inverter start an air compressor?
faqs.a: Usually, for small to mid-size compressors. It is rated at 3,000W continuous with a 6,000W peak, and motor start-up surges often run two to three times running watts. A 1,500W compressor fits. Make sure the battery bank and cabling can deliver the surge current, or the low-voltage cutoff will trip.

name: Go Power! GP-SW2000
amazon: Go Power GP-SW2000-12 pure sine wave inverter
description: A 12V, 2,000W pure sine inverter with a 4,000W surge and dual GFCI outlets from an RV-industry brand, a sensible replacement in a travel trailer battery bay.
quick: 12V DC in, 2,000W continuous, pure sine. A 12V, 2,000W pure sine inverter with a 4,000W surge and dual GFCI outlets from an RV-industry brand, a sensible replacement in a travel trailer battery bay.
bestFor: RVs and travel trailers adding a 2,000W inverter
skipIf: You will leave the inverter on all day without powersave
verdict: Go Power! is a name many RV builders already use for factory solar and inverter packages, so the GP-SW2000 is a natural choice when you add or replace an inverter in a travel trailer or motorhome.

**The ratings.** Go Power lists the GP-SW2000-12 at 2,000W continuous and 4,000W surge, with a [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/) output. That is the size that runs a microwave or coffee maker from the house batteries without starting the generator. Efficiency is listed at 85-92%.

**Idle draw.** The spec sheet lists a no-load draw of 2.8A, or about 34W, and 0.6A in powersave mode. Left on all day without powersave, that idle draw alone would use around 800Wh, most of a 100Ah lithium battery. Use powersave or switch the inverter off when you do not need AC, and estimate the rest with the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/).

**RV-friendly install.** It has dual GFCI outlets for plug-in loads, or you can hardwire it to a load center. A remote port takes an optional remote so you can switch it on from inside while it sits near the batteries in a basement bay. The input range is 10.5-16V, it weighs 21 lb, and Go Power lists a 2-year warranty. As with any 2,000W unit, plan for close to 200 amps at full load, heavy cable and a fuse at the battery.

Owners like the GFCI outlets and the familiar brand. The main complaint is the high idle draw outside powersave mode. It is the RV pick in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide; the [GoWISE 2000W](/gear/gowise-power-2000w-pure-sine-wave-inverter/) offers the same output for less.
pros: Dual GFCI outlets or hardwire option
Powersave mode cuts idle draw to 0.6A
Remote port for an optional in-cabin switch

faqs.q: Can the Go Power GP-SW2000 be hardwired into an RV?
faqs.a: Yes. Go Power says the GP-SW2000 can feed its dual GFCI outlets or be hardwired to a load center. Hardwiring lets it power RV outlets, but you need a transfer method so shore power and the inverter never back-feed each other. Have an RV electrician handle the AC side.

faqs.q: How much power does the Go Power GP-SW2000 use when idle?
faqs.a: Go Power lists 2.8A of no-load draw at 12V, about 34W, and 0.6A in powersave mode. Over 24 hours, the normal idle draw adds up to roughly 800Wh, so use powersave or turn the inverter off when you are not running AC loads.

name: BESTEK 300W Car Inverter
description: A plug-in 300W car inverter with 2 AC outlets and 2 USB ports, the glovebox pick for laptops and phone chargers on road trips, not for CPAPs or motors.
quick: 12V socket plug, 300W, modified sine. A plug-in 300W car inverter with 2 AC outlets and 2 USB ports, the glovebox pick for laptops and phone chargers on road trips, not for CPAPs or motors.
bestFor: Laptops and phone chargers from a car's 12V socket
skipIf: You need to power a CPAP or anything with a motor
verdict: Most people searching for a car inverter want exactly this: something that plugs into the 12V socket and runs a laptop on a road trip.

**The 300W figure has a catch.** BESTEK rates it at 300W continuous with 2 AC outlets and 2 USB charging ports in a compact case. Through a cigarette-lighter plug, though, the vehicle's socket wiring and fuse limit real output. A 15A socket fuse at about 12V is about 180W in theory, and roughly 150W in practice once you allow for losses. The full 300W needs a direct battery connection.

**What fits in 150W.** A laptop charger (65-100W), phone and tablet chargers (5-20W each), a camera battery charger and a small fan all fit. A hair dryer (1,500W), coffee maker or microwave never will. Current math: 150W / 12V / 0.9 is about 14A, right at the limit of most sockets.

**Modified sine, not pure sine.** It outputs a modified sine wave. Laptop bricks, phone chargers and many small devices do not mind. It is the wrong choice for a CPAP, medical equipment, some cordless-tool chargers or anything with a small motor, which can run hot or buzz. For those, use a [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/) inverter such as the [Renogy 1000W](/gear/renogy-1000w-pure-sine-wave-inverter/), wired to the battery.

Owners like the size and price. Complaints focus on a whiny fan and devices that refuse to run on modified sine. It is the plug-in pick in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide. Do not run it with the engine off for long, or you risk a dead starting battery.
pros: Fine for laptop bricks and phone chargers

faqs.q: Can the BESTEK 300W inverter run a CPAP?
faqs.a: It is not a good match. The BESTEK outputs a modified sine wave, and CPAP makers recommend pure sine or a DC power cord. Many CPAPs also draw more with a humidifier on. Use the machine's DC adapter, a pure sine inverter, or a dedicated CPAP battery instead.

faqs.q: Why does my BESTEK 300W inverter shut off with a 200W load?
faqs.a: The car socket is the limit. Most 12V accessory sockets are fused at 10 to 15 amps, which supports roughly 120 to 180W after losses. A 200W load trips the inverter's protection or the vehicle fuse. For the full 300W, connect an inverter directly to the battery.

name: Renogy 2000W Pure Sine Inverter
description: Renogy's 12V, 2,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 4,000W peak and 3 AC outlets, the step up for microwaves and coffee makers in a Renogy-based van build.
quick: 12V DC in, 2,000W continuous, pure sine. Renogy's 12V, 2,000W continuous pure sine inverter with a 4,000W peak and 3 AC outlets, the step up for microwaves and coffee makers in a Renogy-based van build.
bestFor: Van and trailer builds that need microwave power
skipIf: Your battery bank cannot deliver about 185 amps
verdict: The Renogy 2000W is the natural step up from the brand's 1,000W unit when you want to run a microwave or coffee maker, and it fits neatly into a Renogy battery and solar build.

**Ratings.** Renogy rates it at 2,000W continuous and 4,000W peak, with nominal efficiency above 90% and a [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/) output with under 3% THD on linear loads. It has 3 AC outlets and a 5V/2.1A USB port. That covers a 1,000W-class microwave drawing about 1,500W, an induction plate on a low setting, or a coffee maker.

**Plan for 185 amps.** At full load, 2,000W / 12V / 0.9 is about 185 amps. That means heavy cable on a short run, a fuse sized for that cable at the battery, and a bank that can deliver the current. A single 100Ah lithium battery with a 100A BMS will cut out. Two batteries in parallel, or one with a 200A BMS, is the practical minimum.

**Runtime math.** A coffee maker at 900W for 10 minutes uses about 150Wh; a 1,500W microwave for 4 minutes uses about 100Wh. A 200Ah 12V lithium bank holds about 2,560 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/), so short kitchen loads barely dent it. Try your own numbers in the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/). Renogy lists a 1-year warranty.

Its appeal is how it pairs with Renogy batteries and controllers. The drawbacks are the heavy current draw and the 1-year warranty. Compare it with the [GoWISE 2000W](/gear/gowise-power-2000w-pure-sine-wave-inverter/) and the smaller [Renogy 1000W](/gear/renogy-1000w-pure-sine-wave-inverter/) in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide.
pros: Matches Renogy batteries and solar gear

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Renogy 2000W and Renogy 1000W inverters?
faqs.a: Both are 12V pure sine inverters with efficiency above 90%. The 2000W runs 2,000W continuous with a 4,000W peak and 3 AC outlets, enough for a microwave. The 1000W runs 1,000W continuous with a 2,000W peak and 2 outlets. The 2000W draws about 185A at full load, double the 1000W.

faqs.q: Can one 100Ah lithium battery run the Renogy 2000W inverter?
faqs.a: Only at light loads. At full output it draws about 185 amps, and many 100Ah lithium batteries have a 100A BMS limit that will shut off. Short microwave runs need a battery with a 200A BMS or two batteries in parallel. Capacity is fine: 100Ah holds about 1,280Wh.

name: Victron Phoenix 12/800
description: Victron's 12V, 800VA pure sine inverter with ECO mode and VE.Direct, a compact, efficient choice for vans and boats that run laptops, routers and small appliances.
quick: 12V DC in, 800VA, pure sine. Victron's 12V, 800VA pure sine inverter with ECO mode and VE.Direct, a compact, efficient choice for vans and boats that run laptops, routers and small appliances.
bestFor: Vans and boats running laptops, routers and small appliances
skipIf: You need to run a microwave or kettle
specs: VE.Direct port, ECO mode, remote on/off connector
verdict: The Phoenix 12/800 is the Victron to buy when your AC loads are modest and you care more about efficiency and reliability than raw wattage.

**Right-size the rating.** Victron rates it at 800VA, about 650W of continuous real power at 25°C, with a 1,500W peak. That runs laptops, a TV, a router, a CPAP, a blender for short bursts or a power-tool battery charger. It will not run a microwave or kettle; that is a job for a 2,000W unit like the [Renogy 2000W](/gear/renogy-2000w-pure-sine-inverter/).

**Lighter wiring.** At full output, 650W / 12V / 0.9 is about 60 amps. That is far easier to wire than a 2,000W inverter, with lighter cable and a smaller fuse. Leaving it on for small loads is practical too: ECO mode puts it into a search state until something switches on, and standby draw drops to around a watt. Over 24 hours, that can save tens of [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) compared with a budget inverter idling at several watts.

**Monitoring and control.** The VE.Direct port connects to Victron's app (with a Bluetooth dongle) and its monitoring gear, where you can adjust low-voltage cut-off, output voltage and ECO thresholds. A remote on/off connector lets you switch it from inside. The output is a clean [pure sine wave](/glossary/pure-sine-wave/).

Its appeal is low idle draw and Victron's reputation for long service. The drawback is the price per watt. If you need more headroom, the [Victron Phoenix 12/1200](/gear/victron-phoenix-12-1200-inverter/) adds about 350W; see the full field in our [best power inverter](/best-power-inverter/) guide.
pros: ECO mode cuts standby draw to about a watt
About 60A at full load keeps wiring light
cons: App access needs a separate dongle

faqs.q: Can the Victron Phoenix 12/800 run a CPAP and a fridge?
faqs.a: Yes, for most models. It delivers about 650W continuous with a 1,500W peak. A CPAP uses 30 to 60W and a small 120V fridge runs at 60 to 150W with a short start-up surge, well inside the rating. ECO mode may cycle off when the fridge is idle, so set the ECO threshold below its running draw.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 800VA and 650W on the Victron 12/800?
faqs.a: VA is apparent power; watts are real power. Victron rates the 12/800 at 800VA and about 650W continuous at 25°C. Size your loads in watts and stay under 650W for continuous use. Short surges up to 1,500W, such as motor starts, are covered by the peak rating.
